USMLE-style practice · Pathology

Receptor-triggered apoptosis

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

Activated lymphocytes display Fas ligand and contact cells expressing Fas. The target cells activate a death-inducing signaling complex and an initiator caspase before fragmenting. Which event is most directly responsible for starting this death pathway?

  1. Engagement of a cell-surface death receptor
  2. Mechanical tearing of the plasma membrane
  3. Lipase release into adjacent adipose tissue
  4. Precipitation of calcium in extracellular collagen
  5. Failure of lysosomal iron storage
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Engagement of a cell-surface death receptor

Fas ligation triggers the extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway.

Understanding the options

Engagement of a cell-surface death receptor
Fas ligation triggers the extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway.
Mechanical tearing of the plasma membrane
The scenario describes receptor signaling rather than traumatic rupture.
Lipase release into adjacent adipose tissue
This causes enzymatic fat necrosis rather than Fas signaling.
Precipitation of calcium in extracellular collagen
Calcification does not initiate the described receptor complex.
Failure of lysosomal iron storage
Iron storage abnormalities do not explain Fas-dependent initiation.
